solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: United French gentlemen to stop expert crook

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters are pushed into the middle of another word

parts.note: a crack shot is an expert one
U is the standard abbreviation for United in football team names
MM abbreviates messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: A gang of Frenchmen from United team up to foil a skilled swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal, which 'expert' seems to describe; it is really a shepherd's stick, the Scots word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A crummack is a Scots word for a shepherd's staff with a hooked head, the kind of stick known as a crook.

clue.text: Charlie lives with infestation of rodents, bedbugs etc

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: an infestation sits inside its host, so one word is lodged within another

parts.note: to live is to be, so lives is 'is'
mice are typical rodents

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie lives in a home overrun by mice and bedbugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cimex is the Latin genus name for the bedbug, and its plural is the answer; 'etc' widens the definition to related species.
explanation.definitionFit: Cimices is the plural of cimex, the genus of blood-sucking insects that includes the common bedbug and its relatives.

clue.text: Takes title from strong man lacking aspiration nocturnally

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy H sound, so lacking it means that letter is dropped

parts.note: a hunk is a strong, muscular man
nights, as an adverb, means at night

explanation.surface: A night-time robber steals a title from a muscleman who has lost his breath.
explanation.walkthrough: Aspiration is the conventional name for H, so HUNK loses it. Nights as an adverb (as in 'he works nights') gives the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: To unknight someone is to strip them of a knighthood, depriving the person of the honorific Sir.

clue.text: End up holding head: it's uppermost in triviality

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece wraps around another
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: in a down entry the uppermost letter of a word is its first one

parts.note: the first letter of it

explanation.surface: Someone ends up cradling their head in despair over a trivial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: AIM reads upward as MIA and holds NUT plus the I from the top of 'it'. 'End up' sounds like a phrasal verb but is two separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A minutia is a small, precise or trifling detail, so the word names a single trivial point.

clue.text: Enormous clubs suspended all people

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
something suspended is hung
us refers to all of us, the people collectively

explanation.surface: Huge golf clubs hung over the heads of everyone present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' reads as golf or nightclubs, but it is the card suit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chungus is recent internet slang for something big and fat, popularised by a meme of a corpulent cartoon rabbit.

clue.text: Memoir is hilariously somewhat overdoing the blarney?

definitions.note: a phrase describing the adjective's quality rather than a strict adjective

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of something, so only a stretch of these letters is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A comic memoir that piles on the Irish charm a little too thick.
explanation.walkthrough: Blarney is flattering, charming talk associated with Ireland; the question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Oirish describes a stage version of Irishness, exaggerated and stereotyped, as if laying the charm on too heavily.

clue.text: Colombian forest-dweller circles in which communication expert hasn't succeeded

indicators.note: something in which another sits surrounds it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: two circles, each shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: S abbreviates succeeded, so not having it means that letter is removed

parts.note: a linguist is an expert in language and communication

explanation.surface: A forest creature in Colombia runs rings round a failed communicator.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded, so LINGUIST drops it and sits between the two O's.
explanation.definitionFit: The olinguito is a small raccoon-family mammal of Andean cloud forests, formally identified as a species only in 2013.

clue.text: Sanguine but hesitant when Republican replaces Democrat

indicators.note: replacing means one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: someone dubious is doubtful and hesitant
R is the abbreviation for Republican
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A US voter is optimistic yet wavering after switching from Democrat to Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanguine' looks like hopeful, but here it is the older sense of blood-red.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubious means ruby-coloured, and sanguine in its original sense means the colour of blood, a deep red.

clue.text: On the phone, literally ordered popular dried haddock from Arbroath

indicators.note: on the phone we hear words without seeing them written

parts.note: putting letters in order is spelling, so letter by letter ordered is spelled
something popular is in fashion

explanation.surface: A caller places an order for smoked haddock from a Scottish fishing town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' means letter by letter, so the words describe spelling. Arbroath is an east Scottish fishing port famous for smokies.
explanation.definitionFit: A speldin is a Scots word for a small fish, typically haddock, split open and dried in the sun or smoked.

clue.text: Guy that hurt one securing turn of Britain in top sumo bout

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: a turn swings something round to face the other way

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain
ouch is what you say when something hurts
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wrestler cries out in pain after a British turn in a big sumo contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That hurt' reads as a description of the guy but is the cry of pain itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Makuuchi or makunouchi is the highest division of professional sumo, whose bouts are the top-ranked contests.

clue.text: Perhaps navy uniform leaves bachelor a small blister

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: navy is one example of a shade of blue
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degree titles

explanation.surface: A sailor's uniform rubs a single man raw, leaving a little blister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Navy uniform' reads as sailors' clothing, but navy is a colour and uniform the letter U, which departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleb is a small bubble or vesicle on the skin, essentially a tiny raised blister filled with fluid.

clue.text: After Conservative success, you shouldn't have a medal: seek ultimately good cabinet material

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a hit is a success, like a hit record
'you shouldn't have!' is a polite thank-you, and ta is British slang for thanks
gong is British slang for a medal or honour
to woo is to seek someone's favour or love

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of good

explanation.surface: After a Tory election win, a modest politician declines a decoration and seeks good cabinet ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests a government cabinet; it means furniture. Ta is British slang for thanks, and gong British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chittagong wood is a timber from South Asia, named after the Bangladeshi port, prized by furniture makers for cabinetwork.

clue.text: Geneva school briefly uses a dormitory?

parts.note: SCH is the standard short form of school
a dormitory is for sleeping, so someone using one naps

explanation.surface: A Swiss boarding school in Geneva has pupils sleeping in shared dorms.
explanation.walkthrough: Geneva looks like the Swiss city; it is an old name for Dutch gin, from the French for juniper.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is Dutch gin, a strong clear spirit, and schnaps is a general word for such spirits in northern Europe.

clue.text: Ship's speed measuring device with obvious function

parts.note: patent means plainly obvious
the logarithm is a mathematical function, abbreviated log

explanation.surface: A ship's speedometer whose purpose is plain to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as purpose, but it is the mathematical function.
explanation.definitionFit: A patent log is a mechanical instrument towed behind a vessel, with a rotor that registers distance run and so speed.

clue.text: Malay animal was a rat chasing duck around

indicators.note: turning something around makes it face the opposite way

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
to rat on someone is to inform, and an informer sings

explanation.surface: A creature from Malaysia that once was a rodent goes after a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket, and to rat is to inform, which in slang is to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: The linsang is a slender, cat-like carnivore of Southeast Asian forests, including Malaysia, related to civets.

clue.text: Born with no tongue, disadvantage set in stone

indicators.note: something set in a ring sits within it, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone
a loss is a setback or disadvantage

explanation.surface: A child born without a tongue faces a handicap carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in stone' looks like the idiom for fixed, but it tells you where LOSS goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglossate comes from Greek for without a tongue, describing a creature or person congenitally lacking that organ.

clue.text: Sensible double knot never completed by eastern monkey

indicators.note: never finished off with eastern means each word misses its closing E

parts.note: a sensible person is wise
a tie is a knot, and doubling it gives two

explanation.surface: A careful sailor ties a double knot that an eastern monkey never quite finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word loses its last letter E, which 'eastern' stands for: WISE, TIE and TIE all shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: The wistiti is another name for the marmoset, a small South American primate with clawed digits.

clue.text: Is it consisting of traditional start for adagio or allegro?

definitions.text: Is it consisting of traditional start for adagio or allegro?

parts.note: surface padding that sets up the question; supplies no letters
in can mean consisting of, as in 'a novel in three parts'
trad is the short form of traditional

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of adagio

explanation.surface: A musician wonders whether a classical opening should be slow or fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: read as a question, it asks what an old-style opening to a slow or fast movement is.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrada is an introductory piece or prelude, which could open a work before a slow or quick movement.

clue.text: Time very much indeed has split prehistoric stone monument

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: splitting something opens a gap in it for another piece to fill

parts.note: a lot means very much
ay, or aye, is yes indeed

explanation.surface: Time has truly cracked an ancient standing stone.
explanation.walkthrough: AY goes inside 'a lot', after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A talayot is a Bronze Age stone tower found in the Balearic Islands, one of the region's prehistoric megalithic monuments.

clue.text: Remove this native, regressively and deceptively dominated

indicators.note: regressing means moving backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: dele, Latin for delete, is the proofreader's mark meaning remove this
a native son is someone born in a place

explanation.surface: Colonists cruelly drive out a local, having tricked and subdued him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove this' sounds like an order to get rid of the native; it is the meaning of a proofreader's mark. Led by the nose means manipulated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nose-led is led by the nose, controlled through trickery without realising it.

clue.text: I'll goad someone to make equipment for sewers

definitions.note: a first-person description of the noun, spoken by it
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who irritates or provokes others

definitions.note: describes the maker, so the noun is one who does this
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a maker of the pointed tools used by those who stitch

explanation.surface: Someone promises to provoke a person into building drainage gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains, but here it means people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who teases or provokes is said to needle others, and one who manufactures sewing needles is likewise named.

clue.text: Can it, the thing nearby, packaging cold soups

parts.note: 'can it' means be quiet, which is sh

indicators.note: packaging wraps around its contents, so one piece holds another

parts.note: this points to a thing close at hand
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A tin wraps up chilled soups for someone nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a tin, but 'can it' is slang for shut up. C goes inside THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtchi, also spelt shchi, is a traditional Russian cabbage soup, here in the plural for several bowls.

clue.text: Poet about to lay coarse stuff on farm workers

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: a bard is a poet
to lay money is to bet it

explanation.surface: A poet is about to spread manure on the labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like laying something on, but it is a wager; 'stuff' means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Drabbet is a coarse linen fabric traditionally used for the smock-frocks worn by agricultural labourers.

clue.text: Wogan and Dickinson, say, when between Connecticut and Iowa in widening arteries

indicators.note: a thing between two others sits inside them

parts.note: Tel is a nickname for Terry, as in the broadcaster Terry Wogan
Angie Dickinson is an American actress, one example of an Angie
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: Two TV celebrities travel between American states while suffering from a circulatory complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Wogan was a long-running BBC radio and TV presenter, and Tel is the British nickname for a Terry.
explanation.definitionFit: Telangiectasia is the medical term for permanent dilation of small blood vessels, producing visible red spider-like lines.

clue.text: Taysiders' excellent method to traverse loch

indicators.note: to traverse something is to cross over it from side to side, so one piece spans another

parts.note: a way is a method
L is the abbreviation for loch on Scottish maps

explanation.surface: Tayside locals have a fine way of crossing a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Tayside is a region of eastern Scotland, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Waly is a Scots adjective meaning fine, goodly or excellent, used by people from places such as Tayside.

clue.text: Lounges with object of sun worship in focus and claret for tiffin?

parts.note: to loll is to lounge lazily

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a hub is a central focus
Ra was the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Someone lounges about sunbathing and sipping red wine at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin is the Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal, so the question mark points to Raj-era vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Loll-shraub is Anglo-Indian for claret, from Hindi for red wine, the kind drunk with a British colonial lunch.

clue.text: Rubenesque behind with type of stretch-fabric stitching taken halfway around

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps another
halfway means only half the length, so the rest is cut off

parts.note: a zigzag stitch is used on stretchy fabric so the seam can give
aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A curvy figure in stretchy clothes whose seam has come half undone around the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a body part to match Rubenesque, but it is the nautical word. Only the first half of the stitch name is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaftig, from Yiddish, means pleasingly plump, the full curvy figure seen in the paintings of Rubens.

clue.text: Favouring spritzig wine, with parking in wide Russian street

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Sekt is German sparkling wine, and spritzig is German for fizzy
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Someone who likes fizzy wine finds a parking spot on a broad Moscow avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: Spritzig is German for slightly sparkling, pointing to a German wine rather than an English word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospekt is a broad avenue in a Russian city, such as Nevsky Prospekt in St Petersburg.
